app.name: X API v2 developer app (for Composio 'twitter' toolkit)

verdict.summary: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Twitter/X, so you must register your own X developer app and give Composio its Client ID (and Client Secret for confidential app types). The setup itself is quick, but pricing is unclear and any public use depends on X's policy review and several use-case blockers.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for setup and a test connection; plus unknown policy-review time if you distribute to other users
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 1 hour once a developer account exists (X's support page says Free access is immediate after sign-up)
verdict.approval_wait: None stated for Free developer access. No official turnaround for public-use policy review was found; third-party reports say hours to days (unverified).

gates.name: Own developer app, used by your own account
gates.unlocks: Create a Project and App, enable OAuth 2.0, and connect your own X account through Composio.
limits: Only one developer account per X user; it cannot be deleted (f8).
Accounts with suspensions or policy issues must be resolved before applying (f7).
Legacy accounts without an approved developer account see a greyed-out Create an App button (f3).
gates.time_to_reach: About 1 hour after a developer account is approved or immediately, per X's support page

gates.name: Unreviewed app on Free or pay-per-use access (no separate test-user list found)
gates.unlocks: Calls to the X API v2 from your app for your own and any test accounts you control, within tier limits.
limits: Free Projects: 1,500 posts per month cap (f13).
Access tokens last 2 hours unless offline.access is requested (f25).
Per-user rate limits for OAuth 2.0 user tokens, mostly reset every 15 minutes; 429 means limit exceeded (f15).
Third-party reports say new signups moved to pay-per-use prepaid credits from Feb 6, 2026; read caps and starter credits conflict between sources and are unverified (f10, f11, f12).
No dev-mode user cap or test-user allowlist was found in X's docs (f17).

gates.name: Public use by other users (X policy compliance review)
gates.unlocks: Other people connect their X accounts to your app.
limits: X reviews every proposed use of the developer platform for policy compliance (f35).
Uses such as AI-generated replies need prior approval from X before deployment (f36).
Access requests rejected for compliance cannot be reopened (f37).
The correspondence email cannot be changed after submission (f38).
X may audit compliance up to once per year (f51).
gates.time_to_reach: Not officially stated. No marketplace listing review, demo video, logo or domain verification requirement was found.

steps.title: Check your use case against X's restrictions before you apply
steps.detail: Write down what the agent will do on X (read posts, post, DMs, follows, likes, etc.). Check it against the prohibited uses: automated replies, unsolicited DMs, auto-liking, scraping, surveillance, and training AI on X data. X says the stated use case is binding, so describe it accurately.
gotchas: Automated replies are limited to one per interaction and only after the user engages first (f44).
AI-generated replies need prior X approval (f36).
Using X data to train AI/ML models is prohibited, except Grok (f47).

steps.title: Apply for a developer account
steps.detail: Go to developer.x.com and click sign up. Log in with an X account that is in good standing and has email and phone set up. Enter the account name, location and use case, accept the developer agreement, then verify your email.
gotchas: Resolve any suspension or policy issue first (f7).
A single X user can have only one developer account (f8).
Use a team account if several people will manage the app; an individual account cannot later be changed to a team account (f8).

steps.title: Create a Project and an App in the Developer Console
steps.detail: Open the Developer Console (console.x.com) and create a Project, then create an App inside it. Apps must be attached to a Project to call X API v2. On Free access you get one App per Project.
gotchas: Up to 3 apps may exist for development, staging and production of one service, all under one account, with clear labels. Dev or staging apps may not be used for production (f6).
Separate apps for one use case are prohibited (f43).

steps.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 and choose the App type
steps.detail: In the App's authentication settings, turn on OAuth 2.0 under User authentication settings. Choose App type: Native App or Single Page App gives no client secret; Web App or Automated App (bot) is confidential and gives a client secret. Do not enable OAuth 1.0a unless you need it, since OAuth 2.0 is only used with API v2.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Public client (no secret)
values.value: Native App or Single Page App

gotchas: The callback URL in X must match the redirect URI in the authorize request exactly, including protocol and port (f21).
Community reports say a mismatch between the Developer Portal and app code is a common cause of authorize errors (f22).
Confirm with Composio whether it expects a client secret for the App type you choose.

steps.title: Set app permissions
steps.detail: Set the App permissions to Read only, or Read and write if the agent must post, follow, like or send DMs. Changing from Read only to Read and write later requires regenerating credentials and re-authenticating every user.

values.label: App permissions
values.value: Read only, or Read and write (only if needed)

gotchas: Changing from Read only to Read & Write requires you to re-authenticate your App users (f53).

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret once
steps.detail: Find the Client ID in the keys and tokens section under the 'Client ID' header. If your App type is confidential, copy the Client Secret as well. Store both in a secrets manager. Credentials are shown only once at creation or regeneration, and regenerating invalidates the old ones.

values.label: Client ID location
values.value: Keys and tokens section of the Developer Console, header 'Client ID'

gotchas: If you lose the secret, you must regenerate it, which invalidates existing tokens (f52).

steps.title: Enter the credentials in the Composio auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the twitter toolkit using your own app. Paste the Client ID (and Client Secret if confidential). Set the redirect URI in the X App to the exact callback URL that Composio shows in its auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's toolkit record lists a v1 callback path, but its probe used a v3 path. Use the one shown in your auth config and register exactly that (see open questions).
Composio has no managed Twitter OAuth, so the default managed app will not work (f1).

steps.title: Choose the minimum scopes
steps.detail: Draft the scope list for the actual use case. Start from the smallest set; do not use Composio's full default list unless each scope is needed. Write a one-line justification per scope for the consent screen and for X review. Add offline.access only if the agent must run without the user present.

values.label: Scope parameter format
values.value: Space-separated scopes on the authorize URL

gotchas: Authentication alone is not consent; actions such as posting or following need express user consent (f30).
Storing DMs requires express consent and extra safeguards (f31).

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start the Composio connection for your own X account. The authorize request must use PKCE (code_challenge and code_challenge_method S256 or plain) and a state value. Exchange the code within 30 seconds. Confirm the connection returns an access token and, if offline.access was requested, a refresh token.
gotchas: Refresh tokens are exchanged with grant_type=refresh_token and client_id (f26).
Refresh token revocation and inactivity rules were not found (see open questions).

steps.title: Check rate limits and post caps against your planned volume
steps.detail: Compare the planned request volume with the per-user rate limits and the Project post cap. Read the per-endpoint tables for each endpoint you call. For Free Projects, the 1,500 posts per month cap is a hard limit.
gotchas: Per-endpoint tables were not retrieved; the 900-per-15-minute increase applies only to tweet and user lookup on OAuth 2.0 PKCE (f16).
Pricing on the official support page conflicts with third-party reports of pay-per-use credits. Check the official pricing page before quoting costs.

steps.title: Draft the privacy policy, consent flow and bot disclosure
steps.detail: Draft a privacy policy that lists data collected, sharing with X, and contact methods. Draft the consent text shown before a user connects. If the agent acts on X as a bot, draft the operator disclosure and plan to enable the 'Automated' profile label. Show the policy before users can sign up or connect.
gotchas: The privacy policy must be shown before users can download, install or sign up (f32).
Apps must not use names, logos or URLs that falsely imply affiliation with X (f33).
Enable the 'Automated' profile label for automated accounts (f34).

steps.title: Decide whether to offer Sign in with X
steps.detail: Only use Sign in with X if you need it for login. If you do, its App description is shown publicly once the sign-in flow is live, so review that text first. It must be shown at least as prominently as other sign-in options.
gotchas: X may remove Sign in with X or require an Enterprise plan if unique authenticated users greatly exceed the normal level for the tier (f40).
Storing X passwords or asking users for X credentials is forbidden (f41).

steps.title: Submit the proposed use for X policy review
steps.detail: Before you distribute the app to other users, describe the intended use in writing and submit it through X's policy support channel. If the use includes AI-generated replies, request prior approval first. Keep the email you submit with, since it cannot be changed later. Track status in the Developer Portal and by email.
steps.est_time: 1 hour to prepare; review time not published
gotchas: Requests rejected for compliance reasons cannot be reopened (f37).
Requests closed for a missing reply can be reopened by answering the last email (f37).

steps.title: Wait for the X review decision
steps.detail: X reviews proposed uses for policy compliance. No official review turnaround was found. Do not onboard other users until X confirms the use case in writing, and keep records of X data use for audit.
gotchas: X may audit compliance up to once per year (f51).
After API access is terminated, all X data must be deleted within 10 business days (f49).

requirements.item: Developer account with a verified X account in good standing
requirements.detail: Email and phone set up on the X account; no open suspensions or policy issues.
The callback URL in the X App must match the redirect URI in the authorize request, including protocol and port.
code_challenge and code_challenge_method (S256 or plain) on the authorize URL, plus a state value of up to 500 characters.
The authorization code expires 30 seconds after issue.
Access tokens last 2 hours unless offline.access is requested; refresh tokens are exchanged with grant_type=refresh_token.
OAuth 2.0 user-token limits are per user; most reset every 15 minutes; 429 means exceeded.
Must disclose collected data, sharing with X, and contact methods.
No names, logos or URLs that falsely imply affiliation with X.

requirements.item: Express consent for actions taken for users
requirements.detail: Authentication alone is not consent for posting, following or modifying profiles.
Apps performing write actions must follow the Automation Rules; enable the 'Automated' profile label for automated accounts.

requirements.item: Policy compliance review of proposed use
requirements.detail: X reviews every proposed use; applicants must disclose planned use.
Requires X approval before deployment, through the Policy Support form.
Deleted or suspended content must be removed within 24 hours; all X data within 10 business days after termination.

scopes.effect: Read posts. Needed for reading tweets and timelines; X's tier classification is not in the findings.
Post on the user's behalf. Requires express consent and the App must have Read and write permissions.
Read the authenticated user's profile. Needed for most endpoints in X's mapping.
Email of the authenticated user. Not in Composio's default list; add only if the use case needs it, and justify it.
Issues a refresh token so the agent can act without the user present. Without it, tokens last 2 hours.
Read or send direct messages. Storing DMs requires express consent and extra safeguards; unsolicited DMs are prohibited. Avoid unless essential.
Likes must be directly initiated by the authenticated user. Auto-liking is prohibited.

scopes.scope: follows.write / block.write / mute.write / list.write / bookmark.write / media.write / space.read / tweet.moderate.write
scopes.effect: Each is in Composio's default list. Request only if the use case needs it; each adds to what users see and to consent obligations.

blockers.symptom: Authorize fails with a generic error after you enter the Client ID.
blockers.cause: Callback URL in the X App does not exactly match the redirect URI that Composio sends.
blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into the App's callback field, including protocol and port, and retry.

blockers.symptom: Create an App button is greyed out.
blockers.cause: Legacy account without an approved developer account.
blockers.fix: Apply for a developer account from developer.x.com and wait for access before creating an App.

blockers.symptom: Cannot apply for a developer account.
blockers.cause: The X account has a suspension or unresolved policy issue.
blockers.fix: Resolve the suspension or policy issue first, then apply.

blockers.symptom: Agent plan is rejected, or X threatens to terminate access.
blockers.cause: Use case includes automated replies beyond one per interaction, unsolicited DMs, auto-liking, scraping or browser automation, surveillance/tracking, or training AI models on X data.
blockers.fix: Remove or redesign those behaviors before submitting the use case. Use the API only as documented.

blockers.symptom: Plan is to serve many customers with one set of X API credentials, or to have end users register their own apps.
blockers.cause: Service-bureau or rental model is prohibited; multiple apps for one use case are prohibited; requiring end users to register apps can trigger enforcement.
blockers.fix: Get written confirmation from X on your model before onboarding other users. Do not ship a shared-credential or multi-app design without it.

blockers.symptom: Sign in with X is rejected or removed.
blockers.cause: It is not displayed as prominently as other sign-in options, or unique authenticated users greatly exceed the tier's normal level.
blockers.fix: Give it equal prominence with other sign-in options. Plan an Enterprise tier if usage will be high.

blockers.cause: AI-generated content and replies need prior approval from X.
blockers.fix: Request approval through the Policy Support form before deploying.

blockers.cause: X rejected the use case during policy review.
blockers.fix: Rejections for compliance cannot be reopened, so revise the design and plan a new application. Answer any missing-reply email promptly to keep the request open.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth for Twitter/X, so you must register your own X developer app and give Composio its Client ID (and Client Secret if your App type is confidential). Composio's default scope list is broad; request only what the use case needs. Confirm the redirect URI Composio expects in its auth config before registering it in X.

Whether Composio requires a Client Secret for your chosen App type (Web App vs Native/SPA) was not confirmed.

Current pricing is unclear: the official support page lists Free, Basic ($100/month) and Pro ($5K/month), but third-party reports say pay-per-use credits replaced these for new signups from Feb 2026, with conflicting read caps and starter credits. Check the official pricing page before quoting costs.
No official turnaround for developer-account application or public-use policy review was found. Third-party reports say hours to days; unverified.
No marketplace or listing review, demo video, logo, domain verification or minimum-install requirement was found in the pages reached.
Per-endpoint rate-limit tables were not retrieved, so limits for new pay-per-use apps are unconfirmed.
Refresh token revocation and inactivity rules were not retrieved.
No dev-mode user cap, test-user allowlist or install cap for unreviewed apps was found; confirm in the Developer Portal before planning Gate 2 users.
